disease_label_per_paper: Recurrent sepsis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes bacteremia, suspected entry from an infected ischemic toe wound
presentation_summary: 75-year-old man presented with 24 hours of disorientation and fever, with diabetes, severe atherosclerosis, claudication, mechanical aortic valve, prior stroke, and coronary bypass history.
Presentation exam showed temperature 38.1 degC, tachycardia, left-sided finger-nose dysmetria, and tender erythema around the left great toe.
Admission WBC was 9.8 x10^9/L and CRP was initially 7 mg/L, later peaking at 49 mg/L; CT brain and chest X-ray did not identify an alternative acute source.
Two months later he re-presented febrile after a seizure, with temperature 40.1 degC, tachycardia, tachypnea, WBC 17 x10^9/L, CRP 19 mg/L, and a necrotic left great toe tip.

case_notes: Blood culture species, emm typing, and final source adjudication are confirmatory/non-ranking. Rankable evidence retains fever, mental status, soft tissue/toe findings, ischemic wound context, WBC, and CRP.
This case should not be forced into infective endocarditis despite prosthetic valve history because the paper's echocardiography evidence is confirmatory/non-ranking and negative.
